meta.what: The translator patch table: the project's local patches to the open-source Maclator translator, the self-built kernel's versions, and the on-disk edits to Apple files the boot recipes apply.
meta.upstream_rule: The translator changes the project runs are kept on a public branch of its fork (queue/boot-tested-2026-11-24 on willmcginnis/maclator; UPSTREAMS.md). Each change that fits upstream is still offered there as a small, clean change framed around that project's own goals; patch J still needs splitting first. The upstream cut of patch G was merged on 2026-11-10 (de04499f, pull request #12). On 2026-11-23 patch K (pull request #16), four more changes (#17, #18, #19 and #22) and two questions as issues (#20 and #21) were posted; all are open at this snapshot. On 2026-11-24 a commit was added to #22 (the runtime's own sysctl names stay usable in a forked child), and the descriptions of #19 and #22 were revised; read again on 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-26, all were still open with no reply from upstream. The rest have not been posted. On 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 the fork's branch gained R2, Z, AA, AB and some smaller fixes to the translation cache, the event imitation and their tests, and on 2026-11-26 patch AC with five changes from its reviews. The translator built from the branch's tip after that was booted on 2026-11-26 on a display test overlay, in place of the local builds for every program they had been named for but the disk-image control, and every row for the programs it ran held (1 boot), while the Dock, which does not run on it, came late and two programs not on it newly crashed; local builds carrying R2, Z, AA and AB had been booted before.

states.in progress: built and under test, or not yet in the boots
states.superseded: built, then replaced by a later patch

maclator_patches.fixes: Picked the wrong arm64e subslice in 27's fat files; now ranks the subtype
Store-release instructions could show outcomes the Arm memory model forbids (27,999 in 200,000 before)
27's x86 kernel refuses an anonymous read-write-execute mapping without MAP_JIT
An empty-name *at call was rewritten, which broke 27's dyld mapping its cache
Kept descriptor-bound *at flags and the no-follow-any flags when a name is rewritten
A sysroot given through a symlink broke no-follow lookups
An unreadable path pointer crashed the translator where the kernel answers EFAULT
maclator_patches.note: Posted upstream on 2026-11-08, the first of the stack, after two independent reviews; its upstream cut was merged 2026-11-10 (de04499f, pull request #12), and a smaller remainder of the local patch stays in the queue. A local follow-up reports a refused guest read instead of failing silently; in one boot of an engine carrying it, no such report appeared in the error output that could be read (most daemons' error output goes nowhere visible).

maclator_patches.fixes: A '..' after a cache prefix could climb out of the sysroot
maclator_patches.note: Eight corner cases are recorded as accepted coverage gaps (docs/gaps.md).

maclator_patches.fixes: A forked child could hang or die on a lock another thread held at fork time
maclator_patches.note: Large (about 3,750 lines); needs splitting before it goes upstream.

maclator_patches.fixes: Crashed on an unreadable sysctl name; answered writes and hardware-feature names unlike native
maclator_patches.note: Redone as a single change on upstream's current main (2d2f5b3e), with its own guest test, and posted upstream on 2026-11-23 as pull request #16, open at this snapshot. A local follow-up answers name lookups for the sysctl names the translator itself provides: its 14 test cases passed on arm64 and on arm64e under an engine carrying it (1 boot); posted on 2026-11-23 as pull request #22, open. On 2026-11-24 a commit was added to it: a forked child could wait forever on the lock that holds those names if another thread held it at the fork; the lock is now taken around the guest's fork, and a unit test forks while another thread holds it.

maclator_patches.fixes: A descriptor race between a check and the call it guards
A translated program asking about its own code signature got the translator's answer; it now gets its own, using Apple's own validator code
maclator_patches.note: Its first spawn at boot gets no answer from a framework check and falls back (a recorded gap).

maclator_patches.fixes: Adds a mode with no sysroot, for running at 27's real paths
Closed the earlier accepted gaps that turned out to be real defects
Mapped over unmapped space with MAP_FIXED, raising kernel guard exceptions (fatal in a platform binary); now reserves the range first, as Wine, QEMU user mode and FEX do
An anywhere VM map was not rounded to the 16 KiB pages the guest believes in, so freeing one took its neighbour

Rounded every file mapping up to 16 KiB, so mapping notifyd's 4 KiB shared-memory object failed; every translated process's notification registration then failed, and 27's loginwindow stopped the login at its audit step. Now, when the rounded mapping is refused with EINVAL and the program asked for less, it retries at the program's own length (a retry the kernel refuses is still refused)
maclator_patches.n: 4 unit tests; 17 login boots; 2 test boots of each default base
maclator_patches.note: Matches Apple silicon, whose kernel maps the short object. The user session first started with it. On the fork's public branch; not yet offered upstream.

maclator_patches.fixes: Each process kept its own slid copy of the cache; now one file mapped copy-on-write
maclator_patches.n: 396 MB to 19 MB for one daemon
maclator_patches.note: Two later local revisions: each slid file is checked once per boot and then trusted through a stamp, and a file that failed a whole check is refused for the rest of the boot. In one 38-minute boot of an engine carrying them, stamps were written, and all 14 early stamps kept their modification times while more translated programs started, which is consistent with reuse; in the two store directories sampled, the file count rose in one early step and then showed no net growth over the last ten samples (other per-daemon stores were not sampled).

maclator_patches.fixes: R's slid store was kept per home directory, so the same files were copied into each home directory and sandbox container that used it (16 stores in one boot held about 9 GiB of cache files, mostly duplicated slid data, and the disk ran out of space); now, where a root-owned shared store exists, every user maps root's copy, and a process that cannot use it slides privately rather than write a copy under its home; where the shared store is missing or not trustworthy, the old per-home store is still used
maclator_patches.n: unit tests; 16 boots on the login line, 13 of them through a login; 2 test boots of the default base
maclator_patches.note: Its first build booted twice on 2026-11-24, in two arrangements. With nearly every translated program on it, the shared store held one copy (14 data files, about 560 MiB) and the disk did not fill, but no login window appeared. Named for 81 programs on the login path, with another build as the default, the login went through, but the programs on the other build made 140 copies in 10 per-home stores and free space fell to about 2.15 GiB by the end of the boot. A later build, which keeps each reader's own checks of the shared store in that reader's own store, passed the whole test suite; it and the first build each booted once with no login window, in a set-up in which a disk-management service kept crashing (docs/boot-programs.md, diskarbitrationd). In the login boots after that, with the fix named for 97 programs, the lowest free space was 2.33 GiB, and 126 slid files outside the shared store were in 9 per-home stores when sampled, a tenth getting a set later (1 boot); named for about 120, the lowest was 5.71, 5.49 and 5.12 GiB, with four per-home stores (56 slid files) left, written, where the writer was named, by programs on another build (3 boots). In the next five login boots on the display test overlays the lowest was 5.84, 4.55, 5.52, 5.51 and 5.04 GiB, with three per-home stores left in each; in the three login boots on the default test base adopted on 2026-11-25, where it is the default for nearly every translated program, 6.24, 5.23 and 6.36 GiB, with one per-home store of slid data left in each (its writer not read) and the translator's other cached files still kept per home. The default test base adopted on 2026-11-25 uses a later build as its default translator, with an empty shared store: no per-home copies were found at any sample of its 2 test boots, and over about 20 minutes from early in a boot free space fell by 1.54 GiB, against 5.23 GiB for a matched control boot of the previous base (1 boot each). So disk use through a login with every program on it is not shown yet. That every user's processes trust root's copy is a lab policy the owner has not ruled on. On the fork's public branch since 2026-11-25; not yet offered upstream.

maclator_patches.fixes: Refused to load a position-independent image when its preferred base was taken; now slides it as the kernel does
maclator_patches.note: This is what let 27's amfid load.

maclator_patches.fixes: The translator's own memory was not charged to the process's limit
Aborted when MAP_JIT is refused (27's sandbox profile for sandboxd denies it); now falls back to the interpreter
A log-only diagnostic for a failed guest-pointer write
A fallback for a refused guest-pointer write
Writes a kernel out-parameter to guest memory through a pipe when a direct write is refused
maclator_patches.note: Superseded by Y, which the rebased queue carries instead (2026-11-22). Before that it removed the sandboxd failure for a hand-started copy in 2 of 2 boots; in the second, the launchd-started copy was still restarting, though it ran with a trace option the hand-started one did not, so the two were not a controlled comparison. An open race from review stood.

maclator_patches.fixes: The same write as X, by a VM copy instead of a pipe
maclator_patches.note: Built and its tests pass. Carried in the rebased queue in place of X. An engine carrying it has been booted, but what those boots showed is not written up in this record yet, and the control boots of the rebased engine did not test this fallback.

maclator_patches.fixes: Read and wrote the program's memory through whatever name the kernel answered, asked afresh on every access, for the program's own task (in a test on an Apple silicon Mac, repeated asks raised the reference count on the same name until it saturated, and the name still worked; on the x86 guest this is not read). In one boot those reads were refused in every WindowManager process (why the kernel's answer stopped working there is not read), the translator's imitation of the kernel's workloop passed each refusal on as a bad address, and Apple's dispatch library stopped the program on purpose. Now it uses the task name libSystem keeps, as native code and the rest of the translator do, and a workloop state check answers a bad address only for a bad address
maclator_patches.n: unit tests; 10 login boots; 2 test boots of the default base
maclator_patches.note: Refused-read warnings: 1,001 across 125 WindowManager processes in the boot before, 0 in the boot with it (1 boot each), and 0 in the captured output of the default base's 2 test boots and of the 7 login boots since that were read for it. Three new regression tests fail on the old code and pass on the new; the other new tests check assumptions and controls. On the fork's public branch; not yet offered upstream.

maclator_patches.fixes: The translator is an x86_64 program that starts on Apple's x86_64 libSystem, so in each translated process libSystem's start-up ran for the translator as well as for the program. In the four app-sandboxed session agents diagnosed, the translator's start-up asked for the program's sandbox first, the program's own request was then refused, and the program stopped before its main function. Now the translator's own start-up reads the process's entitlements without the App Sandbox key, so only the program asks, once, under its own name, as natively
maclator_patches.n: tests on an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27.0.1; 9 boots, for the five session agents tracked and a test program, TextEdit in 7, and two more programs seen asking under their own names in 1
maclator_patches.note: In the boot before it, four of the session's app-sandboxed agents stopped there (239 crash reports). With it, each process of the five it was given to asked once, none stopped there, and four stayed up; a test program in its app container was sandboxed and refused files outside it, as natively (1 boot). It is not yet given to every translated program, and programs seen on another build in that boot still made a request under the translator's name. Apple's Rosetta runtime is a static program that loads no libraries, so it has no such second start-up (read on 27.0.1). On the fork's public branch; not yet offered upstream. In the 8 login boots since, each process of the five again asked once and all were running at the end; TextEdit, given it in 7 of them, asked once.

maclator_patches.fixes: Some of the translator's own start-up ran after the program's own sandbox was in force, and the program's profile refused it: in WindowManager the kernel event queues the translator makes for its imitation of the kernel's thread pool were refused, and the translator took the refusal for a descriptor (docs/gaps.md, B25). Now the translator makes those queues, and raises the process's memory limit, before the program starts; it never takes a refused queue for a descriptor; and in a sandboxed process it leaves its own stores of translated code alone
maclator_patches.n: unit tests; 8 login boots, for 11 or more programs
maclator_patches.note: With it, WindowManager ran as one instance all boot with no crash report, and the kernel's collected sandbox lines recorded no refused event-queue call, memory-limit call or store access for a program given it (8 boots; each boot's collection had a few short gaps); the session's app-sandboxed agents were given it too (8 boots), and TextEdit (7). It is not yet given to every translated program: in a login boot on the default test base adopted on 2026-11-25, one daemon on that base's default build was refused the memory-limit call (inferred to be a case this patch fixes; named for a build with it in the next login boot there, it was not refused that call), and another wrote 19 abort crash reports, since traced to a model identity missing from the guest's firmware description, not to the translator (inferred; docs/gaps.md, B22). On the fork's public branch since 2026-11-25, followed by five more commits (a message when the descriptor limit cannot be put back, test and comment changes, and two corrections to the translator's imitation of kernel events) that had unit tests only until the translator built from the branch's later tip was booted on 2026-11-26 (1 boot). Not yet offered upstream.

maclator_patches.fixes: When a translated program started a program 27.0.1 ships for arm64e only, the translator started a copy of itself with that program as an argument, so the kernel's record of the child named the translator's file and other processes asking the kernel for the child's signature or entitlements got the translator's (docs/gaps.md, B26). Now, when the kernel started the parent as the program, the translator hands such a start to the kernel, which starts the child as itself; it keeps the old re-launch in several cases, among them a sandboxed parent and a binary preference, and, added from its reviews, a set-user-ID or set-group-ID program, a path with an empty, . or .. name, and a path with a directory spelled otherwise than its own name
maclator_patches.n: unit tests on an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27.0.1; 2 login boots
maclator_patches.note: In a login boot on 2026-11-26 a translated disk-image tool on a build with it attached a RAM disk, its helper started by the kernel as itself with its own entitlement, where the same tool on a build without it was refused for the missing entitlement in the same boot. The pair read the same way in a second login boot that day, on the build from the fork's public branch, in which the three kept re-launch cases added from its reviews were each run once and kept the re-launch, with the same output as when launched directly from the guest's native shell. On the fork's public branch since 2026-11-26, with five changes from its reviews; not offered upstream. It is not yet given to every translated program: programs on other builds still re-launch their children (one seen).

kernel_versions.change: Builds from source; 27's missing exports, syscalls and MIG routines; the CPU-registration wait before lockdown; the foreign-architecture exec option
Fixes to the exec option after two independent reviews; removes a circular wait at exec that could freeze the boot
A translated process may raise its own memory limit, up to a cap
Two exports the recompiled Sandbox kext needs
A sysctl 27's libraries read at boot, added after a launchd abort was seen without it; the build with it booted, and the cause of the abort was not isolated

apple_file_edits.why: Early-boot code assumes arm64; the commpage is never mapped into user processes
apple_file_edits.note: Not needed on the self-built kernel.

apple_file_edits.edit: Main shared cache re-signed at 4 KiB hash pages
apple_file_edits.why: The x86 kernel rejected the 16 KiB hash pages Apple signed the main macOS x86_64 shared cache with (the DriverKit cache ran with its own 16 KiB pages)
apple_file_edits.note: Lossless: the cache's signature is ad hoc.

apple_file_edits.edit: Two device-tree properties made by boot.efi

apple_file_edits.why: 27's x86_64 encoder and arm64e decoder disagree on one field
apple_file_edits.applied: on disk, found by pattern per build
apple_file_edits.note: Also placed in the 27-only root's cache for the display test boots.

apple_file_edits.applied: on disk, found by pattern per build
apple_file_edits.note: Also placed in the 27-only root's cache for the display test boots.

apple_file_edits.edit: Data volume group id written offline
apple_file_edits.why: 27's system volume ships with a zero group id and no tool sets it

apple_file_edits.edit: DriverKit shared cache: eight libdyld forwarding stubs moved up one table slot
apple_file_edits.why: They call dyld's API table one slot short of where 27.0.1's dyld keeps those functions (seven matched by name; the eighth stub's name is stripped and its target was inferred from its neighbours), which crashed the HID driver extension at start
apple_file_edits.applied: on disk, cache re-signed with its own 16 KiB hash pages
apple_file_edits.note: All eight moved, every page hash re-checked. Not yet in the furthest configuration.

apple_file_edits.edit: A DriverKit serial extension moved out of the scanned folder
apple_file_edits.why: It has no x86_64 slice, and its kernel side had no x86_64 build in the collection; with it moved, the registry goes quiet (why it held matching back is inference)
apple_file_edits.applied: on disk, the .dext moved to another folder
apple_file_edits.note: One of two fixes for the registry stall (docs/gaps.md, B18); the other adds Apple's own x86_64 kext to the boot collection and edits no Apple file. The project's default test bases since 2026-11-24 take the other fix and leave this extension in place.
